abilitygroupdescription.p: FIXME a condition is an antagonist ability applied to a PC. All abilities are also keywords. FIXME: antagonistic abilities are driven by the GM. Often they allow the GM to make checks against the targert PC. A Condition is a type of keyword that has a well-defined game effect, and a lifetime. All conditions are keywords, but not all keywords are conditions. Conditions represent temporary modifications to things in game, often to characters, Blind, or Dazed.

FIXME ConditionsSave Ends Save Ends Conditions have different lifetimes. Some conditions typically last for the length of a combat, or until a Save Ends the effects of the condition. Other conditions might be ongoing and terminate at different times. How and when a PC can save to end a condition should be specified on a per condition, or per instance basis. For example text might say: If the character has a fishing net dropped on them they are Prone Agility Save ends with a DC of 12. Saves are made at the end of the characters turn and, if they have multiple saves to make, in any order the character wishes.
The following is a list of some common conditions.

check.name: Save Against Asphyxiation
check.critsuccess: No effect. Make next Save against Asphyxiation with a shift up.
check.fail: Check again next round with disadvantage.

stage.name: Dyspnea
stage.description: Blood pressure rises, and a lack of oxygen to the brain can cause dizziness, confusion, bluish skin discoloration, and involuntary muscle twitching or convulsions. Make all checks shifted down. If the character can breath during their round they lose the Asphyixiating condition. Make a Mettle check at the end of each turn, and progress to the next stage of this condition on failure.

stage.name: Suffocating
stage.description: The character gains the Unconscious and Near-Death conditions and cannot lose them until they can breath again. They cannot reduce their stage in these conditions while asphixiating. They can only increase their stage or remain at their current stage.

abilitydescription.p: Drowning, suffocating, or choking characters have the Asphyxiating condition. Characters lose this condition when they are able to breathe again.
Characters are temporarily immune to asphyxiation while Holding Their Breath, but they cannot start to Hold Their Breath while being Asphyxiated.

stage.name: Helpful
stage.description: Character's make social checks with two shifts up.

stage.name: Friendly
stage.description: Characters make social checks with one shift up.

stage.name: Indifferent
stage.description: Characters make social checks with no shifts.

stage.name: Unfriendly
stage.description: Characters make social checks with one shift down.

stage.name: Hostile
stage.description: Characters make social checks with two shifts down.

abilitydescription.p: This condition represents the disposition of some third party towards a PC or PCs when it comes to social interactions. The GM determines initial attitudes to a party and any changes to those attitudes.

stage.name: Stupefied
stage.description: Two shifts down to all actions. No OOTAs.

stage.name: Dazzed
stage.description: Two shifts down to all actions. Free OOTAs have a OOTA cost in this stage.

stage.name: Confused
stage.description: Shift down to all actions. Free OOTAs have a OOTA cost in this stage.

abilitydescription.p: The character is unable to think or plan clearly, they are uncoordinated and their understanding about what is happening is impaired.

The character cannot see. Four shifts down on perception and ranged attacks which use sight, three shifts down on melee attacks. This condition has the same effects as the Pitch Black stage for the Lighting condition.

check.name: Every Round
check.precondition: At the start of your turn you are Burning.
check.effect: Take Dmg+Rank damage. Make a Mettle Save or you must immediately Drop and Roll.

abilitydescription.p: The character is on fire! They suffer burning damage each round until they can put themselves out.

stage.name: Complete Cover
stage.description: Character is behind something that completely blocks attacks. No damage is taken.

stage.name: Full Cover
stage.description: Character is behing something that completely blocks attacks, such as a wall. But the character is sticking their head out to observe, or firing from cover, so they are not completely protected. Attacks and perception checks are made against the character with three shifts down.

stage.name: Cover
stage.description: Character is behind something that offers protection from attacks, for example a turned over table, a medium sized tree, hard corners of a building, or a gravestone. Attacks and perception checks are made against the character with two shifts down.

stage.name: Partial Cover
stage.description: The character is behind something that offers partial protection from attacks, for example chairs, a wagon, or another character. Attacks and perception checks are made against the character with one shift down.

stage.name: Concealment
stage.description: The character is behind something that obscures their true location but provides little or no physical protection, for example, behind a curtain, waterfall, tall grass, or small bushes. Ranged attacks are made against the character with one shift down. Perception checks are made against the character with two shifts down.

abilitydescription.p: Standing next to a character in cover may reduce or negate that cover. For example the GM may rule that when making a melee attack against a character behind an overturned table, instead their Cover is reduced to Partial Cover.
FIXME: damage from blockable area attacks: Fire and Acid. FIXME: damage from unblockable attacks is unaffected (poison gas).
The GM has final say in the modifiers provided. For example the GM might rule that an ice wall provides full cover, but only one shift down for perception checks.

check.name: Escape
check.effect: The character attempts to get free of the grab or break their bonds.

stage.name: Hobbled
stage.description: The character has been grabbed around the legs. They cannot make move actions. Dodge actions are made with a shift down.

stage.name: Grabbed
stage.description: The character has been grabbed. They are Hobbled. They make all physical checks with a shift down.

stage.name: Restrained
stage.description: The character can barely move. They are grabbed. The only physical actions the character can make are Escape, Headbut.

stage.name: Immobilized
stage.description: The character is Restrained. The cannot even perform somatic gestures to cast spells, so they cast spells shifted down one.

check.name: On Your Turn
check.precondition: This action happens during your turn.

abilitydescription.p: Holding your breath confers some protection against various poison gas, disease, acidic vapours, and other noxious gas effects.

Characters can hold their breath for 7 plus Endurance Rank turns. After which they must make a Free Endurance Save each turn to keep holding their breath, or begin asphyxiating. For example a character with Endurance 3 can hold their breath for 10 turns before they must start saving.

Characters can automatically hold their breath if they are prepared to do so, for example, before running into a burning building. However they must make a save if they want to do so as a response to some surprising third party event, falling into water.
Characters cannot start to Hold Their Breath while being asphyxiated.
The character loses one action point per rank in Impeded.

stage.name: Pitch Black
stage.description: No light. Underground with no light sources. Four shifts down on perception and ranged attacks, three shifts down on melee attacks.

stage.name: Very Dark
stage.description: Night with no light sources, in the countryside with a new moon, in forests at night, or underground with a few candles. Three shifts down on perception and ranged attacks, two shifts down on melee attacks.

stage.name: Dark
stage.description: Night with very few or distant light sources, e.g. dark city streets, underground with a lamp. Two shifts down on perception and ranged attacks, one shift down on melee attacks.

stage.name: Dim
stage.description: Dusk, or dark forest during the day. One shift down on perception and ranged attacks.

stage.name: Light
stage.description: Interior of a well lit house at night, outside during the day. No modifiers.

stage.name: Bright
stage.description: Middle of the day in a desert or snowfield. One shift down on perception and ranged attacks.

stage.name: Very Bright
stage.description: Magical light. Two shifts down on perception and ranged attacks, one shift down on melee attacks.

abilitydescription.p: This condition describes the level of illumination in the area. These modifiers are for sight based checks.

check.name: Stand Firm
check.precondition: The character is frightened and makes a righteous will or mettle check, or rests.

abilitydescription.p: The character makes Mettle and Break saves with one shift down.

ability.slug: There's a big difference between mostly dead and all dead.

check.name: Roll for Near Death
check.precondition: This check is made at the start of your turn.
check.effect: The character rolls on the Near-Death table.

check.name: Struggle
check.precondition: The character may make a Will Check once per round.

check.name: Divine Intervention
check.critsuccess: Apply the "I'm Fine" result from the Near-Death table.
check.righteoussuccess: Apply the "Flesh Wound" result from the Near-Death table.
check.success: Apply the "Where am I" result from the Near-Death table.

ability.abilitydescription:
The player must make rolls on the Near-Death table for the character each round until the condition is removed of their character dies. Characters who are Near-Death have the condition and will usually have the condition as well.
Characters who are Near Death are effectively too hurt and too weak to defend themselves or do too much and are in danger of dying. Enemy combatants will tend to leave characters who are Near Death alone until after combat ends when they can be dispatched, eaten, saved for later, ransomed or sold into slavery.
Divine intervention is a special rule where a character may be spared by an intervention from Mithras or their patron before they die. As a character is just about to die they may make a Divine Intevention Save. If successful the powerful entity intervenes, usually indirectly, on the characters behalf somehow. Particularly religious characters gain a shift up on this roll. If the character has donated to the church of Mithras recently they gain an additional shift up.
Such intervention, when it happens, is never free of obligation and the entity will surely assume something in return. If successful the character gains an aspect reflecting this obligation to the deity. In
